title: Social feed
like: a home timeline like X or Facebook
brief: Every person opens the app and sees a feed of posts from the people they follow. Most people have a few hundred followers, but a few have millions, and when they post, millions of feeds must change. The feed must be fast and your own post must show up at once.

clarify.q: Must the feed be perfectly fresh?
clarify.a: A few seconds behind is fine, except for your own posts, which must show at once.

clarify.q: How many followers does a typical account have?
clarify.a: About 200. A few thousand accounts have over a million.

clarify.q: How often do people read versus post?
clarify.a: Roughly 40 reads for every post. Reading is the hot path.

clarify.q: Are feeds ranked or in order of time?
clarify.a: In order of time to start with. Ranking can come later.

notes: About 20 million posts are made per day (approx.).
A post is about 1 KB. Media is handled by a different system.
Notification speed measures provider acceptance. Device receipt is outside this traffic model; check expiry, provider outcome and retries in the correctness trace before claiming delivery guarantees.

hints: There are many more reads than posts. Would you rather do the work when someone posts, or when someone reads?
Pushing a post into every follower's ready-made feed makes reads very fast. But a celebrity with 5 million followers makes one post become 5 million writes. Handle big accounts differently.
Idempotent fanout and restartable progress make partial completion safe. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: The standard answer is a hybrid. For normal accounts, push each new post into every follower's ready-made feed, so reading is one cache lookup. For celebrities, do not push: merge their latest posts into the feed at read time. A queue absorbs the burst of work that a post causes.

designs.name: Hybrid fanout: push for most, pull for celebrities
designs.why: Feeds are held in a distributed cache so each read is one lookup. A queue and workers apply the push for normal accounts. Posts from very large accounts are fetched when needed and merged, so one celebrity post does not become millions of writes.

tradeoffs: Pushing into feeds makes reads very fast but multiplies every post by its follower count. That is cheap at 200 followers and ruinous at 5 million.
Merging a celebrity's posts at read time makes reads a little slower but avoids millions of writes. It is the price of treating big accounts differently.
Keeping feeds only in a cache is fast but risky. A lost feed can be rebuilt from the posts, so the cache is the shortcut and the posts are the truth.
Your own post should be added to your own feed in the request itself, so you see it at once, while the push to followers can happen a few seconds later.
A queue between "post saved" and "feeds updated" means a spike of posts becomes a short delay and not an outage.
editorial.realWorld: Big timelines are commonly built from cached lists of post ids per person, so a read touches memory and not a disk (approx.). Accounts with millions of followers are usually handled apart from the rest.

correctness.prompt: Social feed: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Bound fanout for celebrity posts while preserving read-your-writes. Follower skew makes synchronous fanout an unbounded write obligation. Read-your-writes can be preserved independently of global propagation. Idempotent fanout and restartable progress make partial completion safe.

fields.label: Step 1. A celebrity posts to ten million followers. Materialize every feed immediately?
options: Use a measured hybrid with pull or bounded fanout for large accounts
Synchronously update every feed before acknowledging
fields.explanation: Follower skew makes synchronous fanout an unbounded write obligation.

fields.label: Step 2. The author immediately opens their feed before fanout completes. What appears?
options: Wait until all followers received the post
Merge their committed post into the read path
fields.explanation: Read-your-writes can be preserved independently of global propagation.

fields.label: Step 3. Fanout retries halfway through. What prevents duplicate entries?
options: Unique recipient and post ids plus a durable cursor
Restart and append every entry again
fields.explanation: Idempotent fanout and restartable progress make partial completion safe.

correctness.responsibility: Bound fanout for celebrity posts while preserving read-your-writes.
correctness.limits: The traffic model does not execute this protocol. The checked trace covers its central responsibility; the written explanation is retained for review.

twist.brief: Demand has settled at about 15,000 requests/s. The new monthly ceiling is $52,457. The original burst reserve now competes with the operating budget. Decide which reserve to keep, then test its failure headroom. All data and recovery promises still apply.

design.name: Smaller workload, measured reserve
design.why: Reduce the paid floor for the quieter workload, preserving the required copies and recovery settings. This design was checked through the full event day.
